definition.title: Read a file
definition.description: Read a file's full text content from disk by path. The usual first step before changing a file: look at what it says.

definition.title: Write a file
definition.description: Write text to a file, creating it when it does not exist and replacing its contents when it does. The canonical way to save, edit, or generate a file.

definition.title: Write binary file content
definition.description: Write raw bytes to a file, creating it when it does not exist and replacing its contents when it does. The binary counterpart to fs.writeFile, which encodes as UTF-8 and would corrupt an image or any other non-text payload. Bytes travel base64-encoded because capability inputs are JSON.

definition.title: List the whole file tree
definition.description: List every file and folder in the workspace as a nested tree, showing the whole project layout rather than the contents of one directory.

definition.title: File size and dates
definition.description: Get a path's size, modification time, and whether it is a directory, without reading its contents.

definition.title: Check a path exists
definition.description: Check whether a file or folder exists at a path, before reading it or overwriting it.

definition.title: Copy a file
definition.description: Copy a file or folder to another path, leaving the original in place.

definition.title: Create a folder
definition.description: Create a folder, optionally creating the missing parent folders above it.

definition.title: List one folder
definition.description: List the files and folders directly inside one directory, optionally recursing into subfolders.

definition.title: File version history
definition.description: List the earlier saved versions of one file, so a change can be reviewed or rolled back.

definition.title: Read an earlier version
definition.description: Read a file's contents as they were at one of its earlier saved versions.

definition.title: Read a stored secret
definition.description: Read a stored credential — an API key, token, or password — from the host's secret store by name; the result is the secret itself, so it must never be written to a file, a log, or a message.

definition.title: Store a secret
definition.description: Store a credential — an API key, token, or password — in the host's secret store under a name, so other capabilities can use it without the value being written anywhere else.

definition.title: Chat with a model
definition.description: Send a conversation to a language model and get the reply back as text.

definition.title: Stream a model reply
definition.description: Send a conversation to a language model and stream the reply as it is generated. Same contract as llm.chat, with live tokens delivered as events.

definition.title: Plan a workflow
definition.description: Turn a request written in plain language into a runnable workflow plan.

definition.title: Run an instruction class
definition.description: Run one named instruction class — planner, code generator, validator — against a prompt, using the model and the provider chain that class is configured with.

definition.title: Search across all files
definition.description: Search the text of every file in the workspace and return the matching files with their matching lines and line numbers. This is how to answer where something is, which files mention a word, or where a function is defined.

definition.title: Uncommitted changes
definition.description: Show what has changed in the repository: which files have uncommitted changes — modified, added, deleted, and untracked.

definition.title: Commit changes
definition.description: Commit the current changes to version control with a message.

definition.title: Read a workspace file
definition.description: Read a file's text from the workspace — the same operation as fs.readFile, kept for compatibility, and fs.readFile is the one to prefer.

deprecated.reason: Duplicates fs.readFile exactly; kept so older flows and manifests keep working.

definition.title: Write a workspace file
definition.description: Create a workspace file with the given text, kept for compatibility; prefer fs.writeFile, which also updates a file that already exists.

deprecated.reason: Creates only; fs.writeFile also updates a file that already exists.

definition.title: Flat list of workspace files
definition.description: List every file in the workspace as one flat list of paths, without the folder structure that fs.listFiles returns.

definition.title: What this project is
definition.description: Summarize the project in a single read: language and stack, dependencies, the scripts it can run, version control state, a digest of the README, and the meaningful parts of the folder layout. The fastest way to get oriented in an unfamiliar project.

definition.title: Write the project summary to files
definition.description: Write the project summary into the workspace as CLAUDE.md and .claudeignore, so a terminal agent gets oriented from a file read.

definition.title: Remember a fact
definition.description: Save a durable fact about this project under a key so it survives across sessions and is not rediscovered every time.

definition.title: Recall saved facts
definition.description: Read back the facts saved for this project — all of them, or the one under a key.

definition.title: Open a terminal
definition.description: Open a new terminal in the app and return its id.

definition.title: Run a line in an open terminal
definition.description: Type a line into an already open terminal and run it, using the terminal id returned by terminals.create.

definition.title: Run a shell command
definition.description: Run a shell command or program and return its exit code together with everything it printed. This is how tests, builds, installs, and any other command-line work get done.

definition.title: Sign bytes with this workstation key
definition.description: Sign the given bytes with the host's package-signing key and return a detached signature carrying the public half, so a later reader can check the bytes were not altered without holding any secret.

definition.title: Verify a signature
definition.description: Check a detached signature against the given bytes and report whether they were altered since signing; this needs no key and works on a machine that did not produce them.

definition.title: Read the signing public key
definition.description: Read the public half of the host's package-signing key, so a package can name the key in its header before its bytes are signed.

definition.title: Migrate a workflow document
definition.description: Bring a saved workflow document up to a newer schema version, or report what migrating it would change. Reads only; nothing runs.

definition.title: Run a subflow

definition.title: Browse the capability catalog

definition.title: Export capability schemas

definition.title: Find capabilities for a goal

preview.description: Return the file contents without writing anything.

overwrite.description: Replace files that already exist. Off by default because a regenerated workflow discards whatever was edited into it by hand.

pythonVersion.description: The Python the runner sets up, defaulting to the version this workspace's active environment reports.

written.description: False when nothing was written, either because the plan was incomplete or because preview was on.

missing.description: Why a stage cannot run outside the editor. Non-empty means nothing was written.

preview.description: The generated contents, so a caller can show them before agreeing to overwrite.

definition.description: Run each generated CI step here, the way a runner would, and compare its verdict with the gate the pipeline runs. Reports per stage whether the two agree, differ, or could not be compared

ran.description: False when nothing could be verified; see problems.

agree.description: True only when every stage was compared and every comparison agreed. An inconclusive stage is not agreement.

generated.description: What the generated step said, or absent when it could not run.

editor.description: What the pipeline's gate said, or absent when it could not run.

limit.description: How many recent runs to read.

available.description: False when the remote could not be read at all; see problems.

sentence.description: One line naming the verdict and the commit it belongs to.

alignment.description: Whether the latest run ran the commit checked out here.

failedSteps.description: Steps that failed in the latest run, mapped back to pipeline stages.

foreign.description: A pre-push hook is there and something else wrote it.

current.description: Whether the checked-in hook body matches what this pipeline would generate now. Absent when it could not be told.

definition.title: Read the Commit Graph

scope.description: Which refs to walk. "all" includes every branch and tag; "current" follows only the checked-out branch.

skip.description: How many commits to skip, for reading the next page.

parents.description: Parent hashes, newest-first order. Two or more means a merge; none means a root commit.

refs.description: Branches, remote-tracking branches and tags that point at this commit.

problem.description: Why nothing could be read. Absent when the read succeeded, including when the repository simply has no commits.

definition.title: Read What a Commit Changed

hash.description: The commit to read. Any revision git accepts.

status.description: A for added, M for modified, D for deleted, R for renamed, C for copied.

oldPath.description: Where a renamed or copied file came from. Absent otherwise.

problem.description: Why nothing could be read. Absent when the read succeeded.

source.description: Which patch to read. "commit" needs hash; "untracked" needs path.

hash.description: The commit to read, when source is commit. A merge is reported against its first parent.

path.description: The file to read, when source is untracked.

paths.description: Restrict the patch to these files. Ignored for an untracked file.

context.description: Unchanged lines kept around each change. Pass a large number for the whole file.

patch.description: The unified diff as git wrote it.

files.description: One entry per file in the patch, without its lines.

problem.description: Why nothing could be read. Absent when the read succeeded.

output.description: The retrieval the suite's target answered. Must carry a hits array, which is what vectors.query returns.

expect.description: The case's expectation. expect.relevant names each document that should have come back.

match.description: Which field of a hit an expected value names. One field, never a chain, so a wrong match cannot look like a right one.

k.description: Score only the first k hits, so one dataset can be read at several k without re-running the retrieval.

pass.description: Every declared document came back, and the retrieval ran semantically rather than falling back to keyword.

reason.description: Which documents were missed, or why the number does not measure the index.

detail.description: The field compared, k, the mode, the collections read, the missed documents and the rank of the first relevant hit.

output.description: The target's raw answer — a string (fenced or not) or an already-parsed object.

expect.description: The case's own assertions. An object is checked; a prose string is left for the person adjudicating.

contains.description: Every string here must appear in the answer.

notContains.description: None of these may appear in the answer.

requiredKeys.description: Dot paths that must exist in the parsed answer, for this case only.

note.description: Free prose for the adjudicator, never checked.

json.description: Suite option — every answer in this suite must parse as JSON.

required.description: Suite option — dot paths every answer in this suite must carry.

ignoreCase.description: Suite option — compare contains and notContains without case.

scores.description: json.parse is 0 or 1 and only present when the suite asks for JSON; schema.requiredCoverage and expect.satisfied are 0..1 and only present when something declared them; text.chars is a counter, never thresholded.

reason.description: The first failing check in one sentence, never a raw error object.

detail.description: Every check with its verdict, the answer's length, and whether a markdown fence was stripped before parsing.

definition.title: List Knowledge Bases
definition.description: Report the knowledge bases this workspace defines and what their indexes actually hold. The definition and the index are read together on purpose: a definition alone says what someone intended and an index alone says what a build left behind, and only the pair shows a base that was defined and never built, or built and then cleared. Corpora holding chunks that no base defines are reported and never deleted, because the vector store is shared.

base.description: The definition as written in the workspace file.

corpora.description: Every collection this base owns, its own and its prose corpus.

builtAt.description: The later of the base's two collection timestamps.

orphanCorpora.description: Collections with chunks that no base defines. Reported, never cleared.

problems.description: Definitions that could not be used, each with the reason.

fileExists.description: False when the workspace has never defined a base, which is not an error.

vectorsInstalled.description: Absent when the capability catalog could not be read, which is not the same as not installed.

indexError.description: Present when the index could not be read, so zeros are not read as empty.

definition.title: Define a Knowledge Base
definition.description: Write one knowledge base into the workspace definition file. The include list is replaced rather than merged, because a merge would make removing a pattern impossible through this surface and the next build prunes on the list it is given. Nothing is embedded here; a definition is a file.

id.subject: collection
id.description: The corpus name, lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Also the base's identity.

include.description: Workspace-relative globs. The union of what these match is the corpus.

exclude.description: Removed from the include set, applied after it.

proseCorpus.subject: collection
proseCorpus.description: Where a notebook's markdown cells go. Defaults to the base id with a -prose suffix rather than to the shared doc collection, so two bases do not put their prose in the same place.

topK.description: Default number of passages a query on this base returns.

strategy.description: How this base's files are split, auto by default. It is stored with the definition and a build uses it unless the build names another, so a base is comparable four ways without editing the file.

windowLines.description: Lines per window, 50 by default. The file strategy ignores it.

overlapLines.description: Lines the next window repeats, 10 by default.

definition.title: Remove a Knowledge Base
definition.description: Forget a knowledge base definition. The index survives unless clearIndex is set, because deleting a definition edits a file while deleting an index means embedding everything again to get it back, which on a remote embedder means sending it again.

clearIndex.description: Also delete the vectors this base owns. Off by default.

definition.title: Build a Knowledge Base
definition.description: Resolve a base's globs against the workspace and index everything they name. The resolution is refused rather than built when it comes back empty: the build capability treats the path list as the whole corpus and deletes the chunks of every file the list no longer names, so a renamed folder or a typo in a pattern would clear an index and report success. Both of the base's collections are written in one call, and when the embedder is an endpoint every resolved file is sent off this machine.

force.description: Re-index everything, ignoring the unchanged check.

dryRun.description: Resolve the globs and report the paths without embedding anything.

strategy.description: Override the definition's split for this build. A file whose strategy changed is re-indexed even though its bytes did not, so the rebuild actually replaces the chunks rather than skipping every file and reporting a healthy no-op over the previous split.

windowLines.description: Lines per window for this build.

overlapLines.description: Lines the next window repeats for this build.

resolved.description: How the globs resolved, reported whether or not anything was built.

emptyPatterns.description: Include patterns that matched no file. A corpus is rarely meant to have one.

unmatched.description: Files in the workspace no include pattern named. Counted, never listed.

inputTokens.description: Prompt tokens the embedder charged for this build. Absent when the engine reports no count.

definition.title: Clear a Knowledge Base Index
definition.description: Delete the vectors one base owns. Destructive and not undoable, and scoped to that base's own collections one call at a time, because clearing the whole index would take every other base down with the one that was asked for. The definition survives.

definition.title: Ask a Knowledge Base
definition.description: Ask one base a question and return the passages it holds. Every collection the base owns is read, which is the reason to call this rather than the vector query directly: a base routes a notebook's markdown into a second collection at build time, so asking for the base's own corpus alone reads half of it and reports success. The mode comes back untouched, because retrieval falls back to keyword search when there is no index and keyword hits presented as semantic ones are the one way retrieval can lie.

query.description: The question. On a remote embedder this text is sent to the configured address.

topK.description: How many passages to return. Defaults to the base's own setting.

keywordFallback.description: Set false to receive an empty semantic answer instead of keyword results.

mode.description: semantic or keyword, passed through untouched. unknown when the retrieval named none.

corpora.description: Every collection the base owns, which is what was asked for.

read.description: The collections the semantic path actually read. Absent in keyword mode.

reason.description: Why the mode is what it is, when the retrieval says.

definition.title: Preview How a File Splits
definition.description: Show the units one file would be embedded as, without embedding them. Pass a strategy to see a different split, or omit it for the default. The passages themselves are not returned, only their labels, their sizes and their first line. Comparing several splits over one document is knowledge.chunk.compare.

path.description: Workspace path. The split depends on the format, so this is required even when text is supplied.

text.description: The content. Omit to read the file.

strategy.description: How to split each file, auto by default. The vocabulary belongs to vectors.chunk and an unknown value is refused there rather than falling back, so a comparison never reports two strategies that were in fact the same one.

windowLines.description: Lines per window, 50 by default. The file strategy ignores it.

overlapLines.description: Lines the next window repeats, 10 by default. It must be smaller than windowLines.

chunks.description: How many the split produced, which can exceed the number of items returned.

strategy.description: The split actually used, as a signature such as heading-50-10.

byKind.description: How many chunks each label got. Prose and code do not rank together.

head.description: The chunk's first line, whitespace collapsed and bounded.

definition.title: Compare Chunk Strategies
definition.description: Split one document several ways and report the shapes side by side. It measures chunk counts and sizes and nothing else; which split retrieves better needs a built index and a scored question set, and the answer says so rather than letting a table of counts read like a verdict. Nothing is embedded and nothing is stored, so this is free to run on any file. A strategy that refuses is reported beside the ones that ran.

path.description: The document to split. Workspace-relative.

strategies.description: Which splits to compare. Omit for all four.

windowLines.description: Lines per window, applied to every strategy that uses one.

overlapLines.description: Lines the next window repeats, applied the same way.

strategies.description: One entry per split that ran, in the order asked for.

strategy.description: The signature the chunker resolved, such as heading-50-10.

truncated.description: Chunks that hit the 8000-character ceiling and lost their tail.

refused.description: Strategies that would not run, each with its reason. A refusal is a result.

note.description: What these numbers are not. Chunk shape is not retrieval quality.

filePath.subject: file

fileContent.description: File content as a data URL (binary) or UTF-8 text (ASCII)

schema.description: Where the rendered points came from. `host` means only a decimated subset crossed IPC; `content` means the in-band text was used.

definition.title: Open Lineage Panel

definition.title: Read the Data Lineage Graph
definition.description: Return the workspace's data lineage as stages with what each one reads and writes, merged across every installed lineage engine

readable.description: False when the capability catalogue could not be read, which is different from having no engine installed.

failed.description: Engines that were asked and could not answer, in their own words.

graph.description: Null when no engine reported one.

hasLock.description: False when the engine has no record of a run yet, which is different from an empty graph.

stages.description: In the engine's own order, which for DVC is the order the stages sit in the lock. Never re-sorted.

path.description: A path in the workspace, and the node's whole identity.

digest.description: The engine's own hash for it, when it reported one.

digestCount.description: How many states of this path were seen. Digests compare only within one algorithm, so this is the largest number of distinct values any single algorithm reported, never the size of the digest set. More than one means it changed.

digests.description: Every distinct digest seen for this path, sorted.

digestNotComparable.description: True when this path's digests span more than one algorithm or include an unlabelled one, so their being different says nothing about the data.

kinds.description: Which of the engine's lists this path appeared in.

producedBy.description: Stages that wrote it, so an empty list means this is source data.

roots.description: Paths nothing in this graph produced.

leaves.description: Paths nothing in this graph consumed.

unplaced.description: Items the engine reported with no stage, so they are named and where they sit is not known.

definition.title: Walk Back to the Source Data
definition.description: Walk back from a workspace path or a registered model version to the data that produced it

path.description: A path to walk back from, through the current graph. Not a subject, because this names a query key rather than data the call reads.

model.description: A registered model to walk back from, which needs a version too.

version.description: The version of that model, which needs a model name too.

stop.description: Which step of the walk stopped, when it did.

known.description: False when the graph has never heard of the path, which is different from nothing having produced it.

traceId.description: The editor trace of the training run, on the model-version way in.

runId.description: The registry's own id for the training run, on the model-version way in. Which id space that is belongs to the engine - MLflow answers a tracking run id and a git-tag registry answers a commit - so it is carried and never handed to another backend.

sources.description: Where the chain starts, meaning the reached paths nothing in this graph produced. Data and code alike, because a training script is as much a root as the dataset is.

truncated.description: True when the walk stopped at its depth cap rather than at a source.

via.description: Which route answered the model-version half of the walk. `family` is the registry hub, which reads whichever engine the workspace has; `mlflow` is the direct tracking read, used only where no hub is installed and MLflow is therefore the registry.

basis.description: What the answer is made of. `engine` means a lineage engine reported a graph for this run; `trail` means the run's own audit records named data. Said rather than left to be inferred from which field is null.

data.description: What this run named on the audit trail, folded into data versions. Never joined by time - a run that named a path and recorded no digest is reported as having named it without a version, because nothing in the product observes an edit made outside it.

nodes.description: One entry per distinct piece of data, sorted by id.

kinds.description: The subject kinds this data was seen under, from the closed vocabulary in lineage-subjects.md. A list because the id is the identity, so one path that a pipeline both produces and consumes is one entry.

id.description: The subject id exactly as the record carried it. Not a subject annotation here - this names a row in an answer rather than data this call read.

versions.description: Every distinct digest seen for this data, newest sighting first.

digest.description: The digest verbatim, label and all.

algorithm.description: The label, or null for a legacy digest whose algorithm is unknown.

runs.description: Traces of runs that named this version. Never inferred.

reads.description: Read-only sightings. A version with no runs and a positive count here exists and has no recorded user.

versionCount.description: How many distinct states were seen. The largest number of distinct values any single label reported, never the size of the version list.

comparable.description: False when the versions span more than one label or include an unlabelled one, so their being different says nothing about the data.

unversioned.description: Sightings that named this data and carried no version at all.

runs.description: Every run trace that named this data, versioned or not.
One entry per run that named data, newest first. The other direction of the same join.

traceId.description: Absent on a record the host filed under no trace.

from.description: Which schema the field sat on, input or output. Not a direction - a read and a write record the same shape, so nothing here says which way the data moved.

silent.description: Capabilities whose records named nothing at all. Naming them is what keeps this answer from reading as complete when it is not.

omitted.description: Subjects the gateway's own per-record cap dropped.

droppedNodes.description: Data nodes dropped by this hub's cap.

truncated.description: True when a source returned its whole limit, so older records exist unread.

definition.title: Read Past Lineage Runs
definition.description: Return the lineage graphs of past runs, read back from the audit trail rather than from a store of this extension's own

traceId.description: Narrow to one editor run. Absent means every run on the trail.

limit.description: How many runs to return, newest first. Capped by the hub.

runs.description: Newest first. Empty is a real answer, meaning nothing that ran has recorded a graph.

traceId.description: The editor trace the run was filed under, absent when the record carried none.

atMs.description: When the call was recorded, in epoch milliseconds, which is when it finished.

durationMs.description: How long the call took, absent when the record did not say. The only thing on the trail that says when a run began.

capability.description: The capability whose record carried the graph, which is what ran.

truncated.description: True when a source returned its whole limit, so older runs exist unread.

definition.title: Read Data Versions off the Audit Trail
definition.description: Return the data versions this workspace's runs have named, and which run named each one. Use this to answer which version of a dataset or file a governed run actually used.

traceId.description: Narrow to one editor run. Absent reads every run on the trail.

kind.description: Keep only this subject kind. Applied before the node cap, so narrowing cannot hide the row the question was about.

id.description: Keep only this subject id, matched exactly. Not a subject annotation - this names a query key rather than data the call reads.

definition.title: Export Lineage Runs to OpenLineage
definition.description: Export this workspace's past lineage runs to the configured OpenLineage server, where Marquez, DataHub and Atlan read them

dryRun.description: Build the events and report what would be sent without sending anything.

limit.description: How many past runs to export, newest first. Defaults to the configured maximum.

dryRun.description: True when nothing was posted because a dry run was asked for.

target.description: Where the events went, or would have gone. Empty when no server is configured.

runs.description: Past runs read from the lineage hub.

events.description: OpenLineage events built, which is two per stage plus two per run.

sent.description: Events the server accepted. On a failure this is how many landed before it stopped.

untraced.description: Runs carrying no editor trace, which have no id to derive a run from and were not exported.

stageless.description: Runs whose graph named no stage, so there was no job to file them under.

unplaced.description: Engine items reported with no stage, which belong to no job and were not exported.

message.description: One sentence a person can act on.

error.description: The server's own words, when it refused.

definition.title: Run the LLMOps Process
definition.description: Run the process declared in .punica/llmops.yaml, stage by stage, stopping at the first gate that does not pass. Each stage runs the capability actions it declares and then its suite gates; the verdict is read back from the evals baseline, so this never decides for itself whether a gate passed.

stages.description: Stage ids to run, in the process's own order. Omit to run all of them.

stopOnFailure.description: Stop at the first failing gate. Default true; false records every stage instead.

stoppedAt.description: The stage whose gate ended the run. Absent when nothing stopped it.

stages.description: One entry per stage, in order, each with its status, actions and gates.

voice.description: A voice id; the Voice setting when absent.

reading.description: Whether a sentence is playing or queued.

definition.title: Start Ollama Daemon
definition.description: Make sure the local ollama daemon is answering, starting one only when none is. On most machines ollama already runs its own background service and nothing is started at all. endpoint.description: Base address of the live daemon.

managed.description: Whether the answering process was started by this extension.

alreadyRunning.description: True when a daemon was already up and nothing was started.

serverId.description: Host process id, present only for a daemon started here.

managed.description: False when the daemon was not started by this extension.

reason.description: Why nothing was stopped, when nothing was.

definition.title: Ollama Status
definition.description: Report whether the ollama daemon is answering, which models are on this machine, and what to do next when something is missing. Reads over HTTP and starts nothing, including the ollama binary itself.

models.description: Model names present on this machine.

nextStep.description: What to do next, in a sentence. Empty when nothing is missing.

definition.title: Pull Ollama Model
definition.description: Download a model into the local ollama store, so it can be used with no network afterwards. The download runs in a terminal where its progress is visible, and this waits until the model shows up on the machine. It fetches several hundred megabytes and writes them to disk, so it asks every time.

model.description: Model name as it appears in the ollama library, for example nomic-embed-text. Defaults to the llm.ollama.embedModel setting.

present.description: Whether the model is on this machine now.

alreadyPresent.description: True when it was already there and nothing was downloaded.

via.description: Whether the download ran in a terminal or as a command.

definition.title: Remove Ollama Model
definition.description: Delete a model from the local ollama store and free the disk it occupied. The model has to be downloaded again to come back, so this asks every time. Removal goes through the daemon: when nothing is answering, this reports that rather than starting one. A zero exit code is not taken as proof — the model list is read again afterwards and only a model that is really gone is reported as removed.

model.description: Model name as ollama lists it, for example qwen3:4b. A bare name without a tag matches the tagged model of the same name.
The name as the daemon listed it, tag included.

removed.description: True only when the model is gone from the daemon's list.

alreadyAbsent.description: True when there was nothing to remove.

freedBytes.description: Disk the model occupied, as the daemon reported it.

remaining.description: How many models are left on this machine.

reason.description: Why nothing was removed, when nothing was.

definition.title: Install Ollama

The command runs in a terminal where it can be read and interrupted, and this waits until ollama answers. It runs a package manager or a script fetched over the network, so it is high risk and asks every time. Platforms with no automatable path return a manual plan and install nothing.

platform.description: Node platform id (darwin / win32 / linux). Defaults to the machine this is running on.

started.description: True when a command was written to a terminal.

installed.description: True when ollama answered before the wait ran out.

plan.description: The command that was run, or the manual download page.

endpoint.description: OpenAI-compatible base address of the running server.

serverId.description: Host process id, needed to stop this exact server.

endpointCleared.description: Whether the local endpoint setting was cleared by this stop.

language.description: Spoken language as a BCP-47 tag, or auto. English when absent.

definition.title: Dictate
definition.description: Listen to the microphone until the speaker pauses and return what was said as text, transcribed on this machine. A language whose model is missing is offered for download first, and nothing is downloaded without a yes. listen.description: Keep the microphone open while the reply plays and stop it when the person speaks; false when absent.

stopped.description: The reading was cut short by a stop, a replacing reply or words spoken over it.

interrupted.description: Words were spoken over the reading and it stopped for them.

definition.description: Run a single gate headlessly and return its pass/fail verdict with a reason and the numbers it compared

input.description: Payload handed to the gate capability.

metric.description: What the gate measured, e.g. driftShare or recall. Absent when the gate computed no number.

value.description: The measured value. Null when the metric exists and the run never logged it.

bound.description: The bound the value was compared against. Always reported together with boundKind.

boundKind.description: Which side of the bound passes, because a reader given a value and a bound without it can invert the verdict.

championValue.description: The current champion's value, when the gate compared against one.

definition.title: Read the Metric History
definition.description: What the gates measured across past runs, read from this workspace's own audit records

stage.description: Stage id to narrow the series to. Omit for every stage that ever reported a number.

runs.description: Distinct runs the read saw. Describes the read, not the filtered series.

truncated.description: True when the read hit its cap, which makes every series a tail rather than the whole record.

sinceMs.description: Timestamp of the oldest run in the read. Absent when it saw none.

series.description: One entry per stage and metric, because a gate whose metric changed is measuring something else.

delta.description: Latest minus previous. Absent unless both runs logged a number.

direction.description: Which way it moved in the gate's own terms, derived from boundKind rather than from the sign of the delta. Absent when the gate reported no boundKind.

latest.description: One run's reading. value is null when the metric exists and that run never logged it.

points.description: Every reading this read saw, oldest first, newest end kept when there are more than sixty.

definition.title: Run Pipeline
definition.description: Run the configured stages in order; a failing stage marked stop ends the run

stages.description: Subset of stage ids to run, in configured order. Omit to run all.

stopOnFailure.description: Set false to record every stage's verdict instead of stopping at the first stop-gate.

traceId.description: The trace every stage of this run was called under, one per run.

stoppedAt.description: Stage id that ended the run; absent when every stage ran.

metric.description: What the gate measured, e.g. driftShare or recall. Absent when the gate computed no number.

value.description: The measured value. Null when the metric exists and the run never logged it.

bound.description: The bound the value was compared against. Always reported together with boundKind.

boundKind.description: Which side of the bound passes, because a reader given a value and a bound without it can invert the verdict.

championValue.description: The current champion's value, when the gate compared against one.

definition.title: Fire the Pipeline
definition.description: Run the configured pipeline from outside the editor — a drift report, a schedule, a commit hook or an MCP client — and record who asked and why

source.description: Who fired it, e.g. drift, schedule, commit, or a client's name. Recorded verbatim.

reason.description: Why, in the caller's own words. Recorded verbatim; this is what makes an unattended run auditable afterwards.

stages.description: Stage ids to run instead of the configured triggers.stages. Omit to use the file's answer.

definition.title: Configure a Pipeline Stage
definition.description: Write a stage's input into .punica/mlops.yaml: the bar a gate is measured against, the paths it reads, the options its engine takes. Every field is checked against the declaration of the capability the stage dispatches to, so a name the engine would silently ignore is refused instead of written

stageId.description: The stage to configure, as it is named in .punica/mlops.yaml.

input.description: The fields to write into that stage's input. A field set to null is removed from the file, which puts it back to the engine's own default.

capability.description: The capability this stage dispatches to, whose declaration the fields were checked against.

removed.description: Fields this call took out of the file.

input.description: The stage's whole input as the file carries it after the write, read back from disk.

definition.title: Remove a Pipeline Stage
definition.description: Take one stage out of .punica/mlops.yaml as a document edit, leaving every comment and untouched line as it was. Removing the last declared stage leaves the file runnable when a provider is still bound, and the answer says so

stageId.description: The stage to remove, as it is named in .punica/mlops.yaml.

remaining.description: The stage ids the file still declares, in order.

implicitRunRemains.description: True when no stages are declared but a bound provider keeps the DAG runnable as one implicit stage.

triggerSubsetTrimmed.description: True when the trigger subset named the removed stage and stopped naming it in the same write.

definition.title: Move a Pipeline Stage
definition.description: Move one stage up or down by one position in .punica/mlops.yaml; the order is the flow, so this changes what runs before what. A stage already at the end it is pushed toward is refused with the reason named

stageId.description: The stage to move, as it is named in .punica/mlops.yaml.

direction.description: One position toward the start (up) or the end (down).

order.description: The stage ids as the file now declares them, in order.

definition.title: Configure the Pipeline Triggers
definition.description: Write the triggers block of .punica/mlops.yaml: whether a reported drift retrains, and which stages a fired trigger runs. A subset naming a stage the file does not declare is refused, and an empty subset is refused because it would fire nothing while reading as configured

onDrift.description: retrain or ignore; null removes the key, which reads back as ignore.

stages.description: Stage ids a fired trigger runs; null removes the subset so a trigger runs the whole pipeline.

onDrift.description: The effective value after the write, read back from the file.

definition.title: Create the MLOps Pipeline File
definition.description: Create .punica/mlops.yaml as a commented starter from what was chosen: an engine binding, checks, or both. A file that already exists is refused rather than overwritten, and every chosen engine and check is confirmed against the capability catalog before anything is written

provider.description: The pipeline engine to bind, by its provider name (dvc). Omit for a checks-only pipeline that runs its gates and no DAG.

gates.description: The checks to declare, in order, each naming the gate capability it dispatches to. An id left out defaults to the engine's own name, and settings are checked against the capability's declaration.

capability.description: The gate capability the check dispatches to (mlops.pandera.validate).

id.description: The stage id the file will carry. Defaults to the engine's name.

input.description: The check's settings, checked against the capability's declaration before anything is written.

path.description: Where the file was written (.punica/mlops.yaml).

provider.description: The engine binding as the file carries it, empty when none was chosen.

stages.description: The stage ids the file declares, in order.

summary.description: What was created, in one sentence.

definition.title: Train a Model from One Sentence
definition.description: Train a model from one sentence: choose the data file and the target column, write src/train.py, make the workspace a DVC repository, add the train stage, create .punica/mlops.yaml and run the pipeline. The plan is checked against the real files and columns before anything is written, missing Python packages are reported with the call that installs them, and the answer carries the metrics the training printed

directive.description: What to train, in plain words (predict the Survived column of data/titanic.csv).

data.description: Leave this out unless the exact path of an existing .csv file is known; the directive alone is enough and the file is found from it.

target.description: The column to predict, as the file spells it. Leave this out unless it is known; it is read from the directive.

task.description: classification or regression. Decided from the target when omitted.

run.description: Set false to write the pipeline without training. Trains by default.

ok.description: True when the model was trained, or with run false when the pipeline was written.

state.description: needs-packages when the Python environment lacks what training imports, run-failed when the pipeline was written and its training did not pass; absent otherwise.

run.description: What the training run came to, with the metrics the script printed. Absent when nothing was run.

plan.description: The data file, target column, task, experiment and model name the pipeline was written for.

files.description: The files this call wrote or found, each with what happened to it.

next.description: The call that moves this forward when there is one, the install when packages are missing and the run when it was not made or failed, with its input.

summary.description: What was set up or what is missing, in one sentence.

definition.title: Add a Pipeline Stage
definition.description: Add one stage to .punica/mlops.yaml as a document edit, leaving every comment and untouched line as it was. A check lands before the first pipeline step because a contract that runs after training has guarded nothing, and its capability and settings are confirmed against the catalog before anything is written

capability.description: The gate capability the check dispatches to. A pipeline step names none, because it dispatches to the bound engine.

kind.description: gate or pipeline. Defaults to gate when a capability is named.

id.description: The stage id the file will carry. Defaults to the engine's name for a gate and to train for a pipeline step.

title.description: The display name a person reads. Optional; the stage shows its id without one.

input.description: The stage's settings, checked against the declaration of the capability it dispatches to.

onFailure.description: stop or continue. Defaults to stop.

capability.description: The capability the stage dispatches to, null for a pipeline step.

before.description: The stage this one was placed in front of, absent when it was appended.

order.description: The stage ids the file declares after the write, in order.

definition.title: Bind the Pipeline Engine
definition.description: Write which engine runs the DAG (pipeline.provider in .punica/mlops.yaml) as a document edit. An engine the catalog does not list as installed is refused with the installed ones named, and null removes the binding so only the checks run

provider.description: The engine's provider name (dvc), or null to remove the binding.
The binding as the file carries it after the write, empty when it was removed.

definition.title: Rename a Pipeline Stage

stageId.description: The stage to rename, as it is named in .punica/mlops.yaml.

title.description: The display name a person reads, or null to clear it.

definition.title: Plan the Pipeline for CI
definition.description: Ask every stage's provider what it runs outside the editor — the driver files, the pip requirements and the secrets a generated workflow would need. Reports what cannot run rather than pretending it can

complete.description: True only when every stage exported a runnable form. A generator must refuse to write a workflow otherwise.

missing.description: Why each stage cannot run outside the editor.

install.description: pip requirements the whole workflow needs, deduplicated.

step.description: How the stage runs — a driver plus a JSON request, or a plain command.

definition.title: Rank Parameters by Importance
definition.description: Which parameter moved the objective across a set of runs, as an adjusted share of the objective's spread

runs.description: One entry per run or trial. Whoever holds the table builds it; this capability reads no store.

label.description: How the run is named on screen. Never read as data.

params.description: What was set for that run. MLflow records these as strings, so a value that parses as a number is compared as one.

metrics.description: What came out. Only the objective is read.

objective.description: Which metric is the point. There is no default, because guessing it ranks parameters against a number nobody chose.

direction.description: Which way is better. It decides which end of a parameter's range is called best and never changes a share.

method.description: The estimator, named in the answer so a reader never has to guess which one produced the number.

scored.description: Rows that reported the objective. Only these were measured.

balanced.description: True when every measured parameter's values occur equally often. An unbalanced set is observational, so a share describes these runs rather than the parameter.

levels.description: Distinct values among the scored runs.

share.description: Adjusted share of the objective's variance, 0 to 1. Never rises with the number of values on its own.

belowResidual.description: True when the parameter explains less than these runs leave unexplained, which is not the same as not having been measured.

spread.description: Best mean minus worst mean, in the objective's own units.

excluded.description: Parameters that carry no share, each with the reason. A parameter that could not be measured is never reported as a zero.

refusal.description: Present when nothing could be measured, and it says what was missing.

path.subject: dataset

definition.title: Run Sweep

jobs.description: How many trials to run at once. Capped at 32; the engine may run fewer and never runs more.

queued.description: DVC's generated name for every trial this call queued.

started.description: False when the points were queued and the workers could not be started.

refused.description: Points dropped rather than mangled, each with the reason.

parameters.description: What the pipeline declares it takes. Empty is a real answer, and means a sweep has nothing to vary.

definition.description: Bring one trial's parameters into the workspace so the pipeline can be run over them

trial.description: The trial's name, as reported by mlops.dvc.trials.

kill.description: Interrupt the trial in flight instead of letting it finish.

definition.description: Name every stage dvc.yaml already declares, in the file's own order. A workspace with no pipeline file answers with an empty list, since that is the state before the first stage rather than a failure.

already.description: True when the workspace already was a DVC repository.

scm.description: Whether the repository sits on git, absent when nothing was created.

name.description: Stage name. Letters, digits, underscore and hyphen.

cmd.description: The command the stage runs, as a shell line.

deps.description: Paths the command reads. A path an earlier stage produces is allowed and is what makes the DAG.

outs.description: Paths the command writes, tracked in the DVC cache.

metrics.description: Output files DVC reads as metrics.

plots.description: Output files DVC reads as plots.

wdir.description: Directory the command runs in, relative to the repository root.

desc.description: One line describing the stage. Written once — DVC keeps the first one even under force.

force.description: Replace an existing stage, including everything it declared.

refusal.description: DVC's own sentence when it declined, absent when it wrote.

traceId.description: The training run's trace, or null when the version was registered outside the editor.

version.description: The version the stage should point at

alias.description: The stage to move, such as champion

changed.description: False when the stage already pointed here, which GTO refuses and the hub calls a no-op.

definition.title: Open Drift Panel

definition.title: Measure Data Drift
definition.description: Compare a dataset against a reference dataset and report which columns have drifted. This is the engine behind an MLOps drift gate; it reads both datasets and writes nothing unless an HTML report path is given

reference.description: Workspace path to the reference dataset — the data the model was trained against (csv, tsv, parquet, json).

current.description: Workspace path to the dataset to compare against the reference.

columns.description: Compare only these columns. Omit to compare every column the two datasets share.

driftShare.description: The share of drifted columns that counts as dataset drift, 0..1. Evidently's own default is 0.5.

truncated.description: True when a source returned its whole read limit, so older records exist unread.

actors.description: Every actor that made a root call, with how many runs each one has.

runs.description: Newest first. Each run is the calls that share one trace id, as a tree.

root.description: The capability the run is, which is the call whose parent is outside the run, not the earliest record.

startedAt.description: The root's timestamp minus its duration, because the audit timestamp is a completion.

tree.description: The run's calls nested by span, siblings in the order they began. An agent loop's turns are nodes of kind `turn` so tool calls hang from the turn that made them; a turn is not a call and is not counted. Each node carries `kind`, `verdict`, `beganAt`, its `call` (with `source`, `subjects`, and `io` when asked) and `children`.

definition.title: Read Recent Tracking Events
definition.description: Read the recent audit ring and summarize it by kind, optionally filtered by correlationId, kind or free text.

correlationId.description: Follow one correlation or trace chain.

kind.description: Keep only events of this envelope kind.

text.description: Keep only events whose name or payload contains this text.

limit.description: How many of the most recent matching events to return, 1-500. The totals always count every match.

totals.description: Counts across every matching event, not just the returned ones.

recent.description: The most recent matching events, oldest first.

definition.title: Open System Console
definition.description: Open the system diagnostics console (Trace, Health and Capabilities) and optionally focus a traceId/correlationId.

schema.description: What the console was opened on.

definition.title: Open Trace Viewer
definition.description: Open the console on its Trace tab and optionally focus a traceId/correlationId.

schema.description: What the trace tab was opened on.

definition.title: Embed Text
definition.description: Turn a batch of texts into vectors through the configured embedder. This is the only embedding path in the product; nothing reaches a model or an endpoint around it. The signature is plural on purpose — a capability call traverses the whole gateway pipeline, so embedding one chunk at a time would put governance in an inner loop. When the embedder is an endpoint every call sends its texts off this machine.

texts.description: The texts to embed, in order. The returned vectors match this order.

vectors.description: One vector per input text, same order, each of length dim.

modelId.description: Identity of the embedding space these vectors belong to. Vectors from two model ids are not comparable.

servedModelId.subject: model
servedModelId.description: The model that answered, as the engine names it. Absent when the engine does not say. This is not modelId above — that one is the configured space and decides collection names, this one is what ran.

inputTokens.description: Prompt tokens the engine charged for this batch. Absent when the engine reports no count, which is not the same as a batch that cost nothing.

source.description: hash or endpoint — which embedder actually produced these.

definition.title: Embedder Status
definition.description: Report which embedder is configured, the embedding space it names, the vector length, and — when it is remote — the address material would be sent to and whether a token was found. Reads configuration only; sends nothing.

remote.description: True when using the embedder means sending text off this machine.

endpointUrl.description: Present when remote. Shown so the egress is inspectable without a send.

collectionSuffix.description: The modelId and dim part of a collection name. A change here addresses a different collection rather than corrupting the current one.

nextStep.description: What to do next, in a sentence. Neither embedder source onboards itself yet, so this says what is missing instead of leaving an empty field to guess at.

problems.description: Configuration errors that would make an embed call fail, reported without making one.

definition.title: Test Embedder
definition.description: Embed one short probe string and report whether the embedder answered, how long it took and what vector length came back. On a remote embedder this is a real request to the configured address, which is why it is a deliberate action and not something status does on its own.

reason.description: Why the test failed, when it did.

definition.title: Split a File into Chunks
definition.description: Split a file into the units that get embedded, under one of four strategies. Notebooks split by cell, because that is the unit a person thinks in and an assistant should quote back; everything else gets an overlapping line window so a passage straddling a boundary is still reachable from one side. That pair is the auto strategy and it is the default. Paragraph splits on blank lines, heading splits markdown into its sections, and file makes one chunk of the whole document, which is the baseline the other three are worth measuring against. Each chunk is labelled prose or code. This classifies content; it does not choose which collection anything lands in.

path.description: Workspace path. The split depends on the format, so this is required even when text is supplied.

text.description: The content. Omit to read the file, which makes this a read rather than a pure call.

sourceKind.description: workspace (the default) or external for a document read in the renderer.

strategy.description: Which split to use. The vocabulary is closed and an unknown value is refused rather than treated as auto, because a silent fallback would report a comparison between two strategies that were the same one.

windowLines.description: Lines per window, 50 by default. The file strategy ignores it.

overlapLines.description: Lines the next window repeats, 10 by default. It must be smaller than windowLines, or every window advances by a single line and the file is embedded many times over.

id.description: Derived from source kind, path and position, so re-indexing replaces rather than duplicates.

kind.description: prose or code. Prose and code do not belong in the same ranking.

cell.description: Notebook cell index, when the chunk came from one.

truncated.description: The chunk hit the 8000-character ceiling and lost its tail.

strategy.description: The strategy actually used, as a signature such as heading-50-10.

definition.title: Build the Index
definition.description: Build the semantic search index: chunk, embed and store a set of files.

corpus.subject: collection
corpus.description: The collection this build owns, e.g. doc or code.

paths.description: Every path the corpus contains. This list is the corpus, which is why anything missing from it is removed.

force.description: Re-index everything, ignoring the unchanged check.

proseCorpus.description: Where prose chunks go. doc by default, so a notebook's markdown cells do not compete with its code cells for the same slots. Pass the same value as corpus to keep them together.

prune.description: Delete chunks for files the index has and paths does not. On by default. Turn it off for a partial build, and know that dead chunks then survive and come back as results.

strategy.description: How to split each file, auto by default. A file whose strategy changed is re-indexed even though its bytes did not, because otherwise the build would skip it and leave the previous strategy's chunks in an index it reported as freshly built.

windowLines.description: Lines per window, 50 by default. The file strategy ignores it.

overlapLines.description: Lines the next window repeats, 10 by default. It must be smaller than windowLines.

removed.description: Files whose chunks were deleted because the path list no longer names them.

inputTokens.description: Prompt tokens the embedder charged across every batch of this build. Absent when the engine reports no count.

bytesOnDisk.description: Size of the collections after the write. The input to whether the default store has run out.

fullReindex.description: True when file metadata was unavailable, so nothing could be skipped.

strategy.description: The chunk strategy this build wrote, as a signature such as heading-50-10.

warnings.description: Things worth saying out loud — an unreadable file, a chunk ceiling passed, stale chunks that could not be removed.

definition.title: Store Vectors
definition.description: Write records a caller produced itself. This exists so a pipeline authored on the agent canvas can own its own last step instead of handing the whole build over. Vector length is checked against the configured embedder, because mixing lengths in one collection produces confident nonsense rather than an error.

corpus.subject: collection
corpus.description: The collection these records are written into.

definition.title: Index Status
definition.description: Report what is indexed: chunks and files per corpus, bytes on disk, when it was last built, and which embedding space it belongs to. Reads the manifest; embeds nothing and sends nothing.

corpus.description: Narrow to one corpus. Omit for everything.

strategies.description: The chunk strategy signatures this corpus holds. More than one means it was built in two passes with different splits, so a retrieval score measured over it belongs to neither of them.

definition.title: Clear the Index
definition.description: Delete an index. Destructive and not undoable: rebuilding means embedding everything again, which on a remote embedder means sending it again. A corpus-scoped clear deletes that corpus's chunks by id rather than emptying the collections it touched, because a code corpus puts its notebooks' prose in the document collection and taking that down with it would be a surprise.

corpus.description: Narrow to one corpus. Omit to clear everything this extension has indexed.

collections.description: The collections this call actually deleted from, derived from the manifest rather than from the corpus asked for.

definition.title: Query the Index
definition.description: Embed a question and return the nearest passages. This never fails into nothing: with no index, no embedder or an endpoint that stopped answering it falls back to workspace keyword search and says so in mode, with the reason attached. Callers render one list and label it; keyword results presented as semantic ones are the one way retrieval can lie. Several corpora can be read at once because a notebook's prose is routed away from its code, so asking only for code would silently lose the markdown that was moved out; the scores merge because every collection named here belongs to the same embedding space by construction.

corpus.description: One corpus name, a list of them, or a comma-separated list.

query.description: The question. On a remote embedder this text is sent to the configured address.

topK.description: How many passages to return. Default 10.

minScore.description: Drop hits below this cosine score. Off by default on purpose — values from the hash embedder and from a real model are not on the same scale, so a floor tuned on one is wrong on the other.

keywordFallback.description: Set false to receive an empty semantic answer instead of keyword results. The reason is reported either way.

mode.description: semantic or keyword. Never inferred by the caller.

corpora.description: The corpora this call was asked for. Echoed on the keyword and no-index paths too, so it is not what was read.

read.description: The collections the semantic path actually read. Absent in keyword mode and on every failure path, where the store was never touched.

score.description: Cosine similarity. Always 0 in keyword mode, where nothing was measured.

text.description: The passage itself, whole. An assistant needs the passage, not a summary of it.

preview.description: One line, whitespace collapsed, capped. For lists.

reason.description: Why the mode is not semantic, when it is not.

definition.title: Retrieval Probe
definition.description: The pipeline's self-test. Reads one notebook, treats each cell as a chunk, embeds them, stores them in a throwaway collection, asks a question in different words than the notebook uses, and reports whether the right cell came back. The throwaway collection is cleared afterwards. It also runs the same question through keyword search as a control, so "semantic retrieval found it" is a claim with a comparison behind it rather than an assertion.

path.description: Workspace path of the .ipynb to probe.

query.description: The question, deliberately worded unlike the cell that answers it.

expect.description: A substring of the cell that should be retrieved. Omit to just see the ranking.

topK.description: How many hits count as a hit. Default 3.

keyword.description: Term to run through workspace search as the control. Defaults to the query.

pass.description: Whether the expected cell landed inside topK. Absent meaning when expect was not given.

cells.description: How many non-empty cells were embedded.

keywordControl.description: What workspace search returned for the same words. A probe that passes only because keyword search would have found it too has proved nothing.
